transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, thank you so much for seeing me. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. Um, well, work actually suggested I come in. It's not a huge deal, really, just... I guess I've been having a little trouble keeping track of things lately? Like, I'm a maintenance worker, and sometimes I'll, you know, misplace a work order or maybe forget to call someone back when I said I would. It's just a few little slip-ups, but it's kind of piled up a bit, and they want me to get it sorted out before I'm up for a promotion. I really want to do a good job, you know? Does that make sense? I'm sorry if I'm not explaining it right.

Can you describe what you mean by forgetting things? For example, do you forget recent conversations, appointments, or tasks you were supposed to do, or is it mostly small things like where you put something?

Um, well... it's a little embarrassing to admit, to be honest. I really don't want you to think I'm just lazy or careless or anything. But I guess it's mostly... tasks and things I'm supposed to do? 

Like, I'll have scheduled callbacks to make, or I'll promise someone I'll do a basic follow-up on a repair, and it just... slips my mind completely. And the work orders, too, I just keep forgetting them. It feels like such silly little mistakes, but it's just piled up so much lately that work actually sent me here. They basically said I need to get it handled before I lose my shot at moving up, and I really, really don't want to mess this up. I'm trying my best, I promise. 

Does that answer your question okay? I hope I'm giving you the right information.
Have you been feeling down, sad, or hopeless lately, or have you noticed a loss of interest in things you usually enjoy?

Oh, um... no, not really. I mean, I get a little stressed out about the work situation sometimes, just because I want to make sure I do a good job, you know? But I'm not... I wouldn't say I'm sad or hopeless or anything like that. 

I still really like doing my normal stuff on the weekends and everything. I'm actually a pretty upbeat person, mostly! I hope I haven't been sounding too negative today or like I'm just here complaining... I really don't mean to be a bother or sound ungrateful. Is that what you were asking? I hope that's helpful.
Can you tell me if you've been having any trouble focusing or staying concentrated on tasks, like while you're reading, following instructions, or even just having a conversation?

Um, well... I guess maybe a little bit? I really try to pay attention, I promise I do. It's just... well, like with the digital work orders we use. I'll open one up, and I'm totally ready to tackle it, thinking I've got it all under control. But then... I don't know, halfway through reading the notes, my mind just sort of... slips away? 

Like, I'll hear a noise in the hallway, or I'll start thinking about the next job I have to do, and suddenly I realize I'm staring at the screen and I have absolutely no idea what I just read. It's so embarrassing. I always go back and reread it, of course! I don't just leave it. But it happens more than I'd like to admit. I hope that doesn't make me sound incompetent... I really am trying my best to stay focused. Does that make sense, or am I just rambling?
Outside of work, do you find it hard to stay organized or finish tasks like paying bills, doing chores around the house, or keeping track of personal items?

Um, well... at home, I guess I do okay for the most part. I try really hard to keep things tidy, you know? But... well, I guess since you're asking, it's kind of like how I am at work sometimes. 

Like, I'll start a maintenance job, right? And I'm really good at the actual fixing part! I always make sure the repair itself is done properly. But then... it's the very last part that I somehow mess up. Like, I'll finish the fix, but then I'll completely forget to close out the ticket, or I'll forget to put the label back on the panel, or I'll just walk away without checking back in with the tenant to let them know it's done. 

It's just those little final steps that somehow slip past me. I always feel so bad about it afterward, because I don't want people thinking I don't care about my work. I really do care! I just... I don't know why I can't seem to just finish the whole process sometimes. I hope I'm not making myself sound completely unreliable... I really am a hard worker, I promise. Does that answer what you were asking about finishing tasks?

Do you find that these lapses in attention or forgetfulness happen mostly at work, or do they also occur in other parts of your life, like when you're with friends or family, or during your free time?

Um, well, I think it's mostly just a work thing, really. I mean, at home or when I'm with my family, I don't really notice it being a problem. I try to be very present with them, you know? I want to be a good friend and a good mom, so I make sure I'm paying attention when we're hanging out or doing things together on the weekends. 

I guess maybe sometimes I might lose track of a conversation for a second if we're watching TV or something, but that's just normal tired-after-work stuff, right? Everyone gets a little distracted sometimes. I really don't think it's an issue outside of work. I hope that's okay to say... I just want to be honest that it's really just those work tasks that trip me up sometimes. Does that make sense?
Have you ever noticed these same kinds of lapses—like losing focus or forgetting tasks—in other parts of your life, even before this job or during times when you weren't under much stress?

Um... well... I guess if I'm really thinking about it... maybe it's not *just* this job? I mean, I really don't want to sound like I've always been a mess, because I promise I've always tried my hardest! But... well, I do remember things being sort of similar way back in grade school. 

Long before I had any of this work stress, my teachers would always tell my parents that I was bright—which was nice of them to say! But they also said I was always misplacing my papers, or missing parts of the directions they gave us. And I guess I always needed extra reminders to actually finish my classwork. I'd get started and then just... drift off, I suppose. 

I'm so sorry if that makes me sound like I've never been able to get it together. I really, really try to be on top of things, and I hate that I was like that even as a kid. Do you think that means something bad, or is it okay that I struggled a little bit back then too?
When you were a child, before age 12, did you often have trouble staying focused, finishing tasks, or keeping organized, similar to what you described happening now?

Um... yes, actually. I think I just mentioned it, but... yeah, it was definitely happening before I was 12. Like I was saying about grade school, my teachers were always so sweet and told my parents I was a bright girl. But... they did always have to pull my parents aside to say I was losing my assignments, or that I didn't follow all the steps in the directions. 

I was always needing those extra little nudges to get my work done before the bell rang. I wasn't trying to be difficult or ignore them, I promise! I just... I don't know, my brain would just wander off, even way back then. I hope it's not too frustrating that I'm basically repeating myself. I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right. Is that the kind of thing you were looking for?
